raw:
I picked these on structural grounds rather than by running anything against the benchmark. Three rest on the fact that with edge 0 removed, node 1 is dead, so edits to edges 2 and 4 can't change the output. The others rely on the usual NAS-Bench-201 pattern that adding a conv where an edge was missing gains far more than upgrading an existing op, and that swapping a conv for a skip hurts most.
